sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the Hobbs Act. The law bans using threats to obtain property from others. The core question is whether future business commissions count as property. the side that brought the case argues the law only covers tangible items. The government argues it covers intangible economic benefits.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary of federal extortion law. It determines whether threats to secure future business deals are crimes. The outcome shapes how prosecutors handle business disputes involving threats. It clarifies what counts as property under federal statutes.
